title: Viewport: drag a body with gizmo handles (move and rotate), with a floating control bar at the bottom of the viewport that also takes the buttons now on the right

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Asked for by the maintainer in chat (2026-11-12), filed by an agent for him, at the priority he gave: "issue; enhancement; P4; Ability to move a body by dragging around the window using the gizmos each end of the "axis" should have a small round ball to "grab onto" so we can drag the model in that direction.. Move / Rotate should be tied to in 3D view control bar floating ontop at the bottom of the viewport. We should also move the buttons to the right in the view port to a ribbon "overlay" at the bottom instead in the shape of a gray background rounded corners with buttons ontop of it."

**What is wanted**
1. **Drag to move.** A selected body shows a gizmo; each end of each axis has a small round ball to grab. Dragging a ball moves the body along that axis.
2. **Move / Rotate modes** chosen from a control bar that floats over the bottom of the 3D viewport. Rotate uses the same gizmo (rings or the balls as rotation handles - decide and record).
3. **A bottom overlay bar.** The buttons that today sit at the right edge of the viewport (frame, shaded/wireframe and the others there) move into that same overlay: a grey background with rounded corners and the buttons on top of it, at the bottom of the viewport.

**How it must fit the laws**
- Everything Is a Command: a drag is a PREVIEW while the mouse is down (ephemeral, immediate-mode) and ONE undoable command on release - the same model-transform command the Model page's position/rotation fields queue, never a field poke. Escape during a drag cancels with no history step; a zero-length drag adds none.
- Moving a body changes where the part sits: operations generated before the move must read as stale (as they do when the fields are edited); anything derived from the model's placement (the stock "from model", the raw-stock-only mark of #1094 that is void after a move, fixtures located on the part) behaves exactly as with a typed-in move. No new placement path.
- What may be dragged: models, and (decide, with the reason) fixtures and the stock. The work origin already has its own page; do not move it with this gizmo unless the maintainer says so.
- Picking a ball must not fight orbit/pan: a ball under the cursor wins, empty space still orbits. Handles keep a constant size on screen. Snapping (to a grid step, to 90 degrees for rotate) with a modifier key is a parameter with a default, shown in the bar.
- The number is still there: while dragging, the bar shows the distance or angle, and typing a value applies it exactly (same command).
- Layering ui -> app; MCP already moves a model through the transform command - if a new command is added it gets its MCP tool.
- Pixel goldens of the viewport differ at the next cut; pin the behaviour in structural / interaction tests (handles present for a selected body, a drag queues exactly one transform command with the dragged distance, Escape queues none, the overlay holds the buttons that used to be on the right).

**Slices** (each its own PR with `Refs` until the last): (a) the bottom overlay bar with the existing right-hand buttons moved into it; (b) move handles with drag-to-move; (c) rotate; (d) snapping and typed values in the bar.

Done means: a body can be moved and rotated by dragging its gizmo handles, each drag is one undo step, the Move/Rotate choice and the former right-edge buttons live in a rounded grey overlay bar at the bottom of the viewport, and nothing about placement can be changed that the Model page's fields could not change.
